Validation summary: Exp15 fixes `4.1`, `4.2`, and `4.5` are present in the current code. `4.3` should be reopened. `4.4` is only partial. `4.6` should be reopened because the novelty filter can still hide real new findings before they reach per-model yield.

FINDING_ID: MM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: In [dynamic_management.py#L805](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L805), PM is excluded from admissible task assignment when `K > 1`, but [_redundancy_target](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L827) still targets `K` reviewers for critical tasks. I verified a 3-model case gives `target=3` and `admissible=2`, so the “no fix needed” closure for Exp15 `4.3` is mathematically inconsistent: the target is impossible by construction.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Make redundancy and admissibility use the same reviewer universe. Simplest fix: clamp target by admissible reviewer count before feasibility checks and allocation, or explicitly allow PM on critical tasks if “all models” is the intended semantics.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.56  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.34  
DESCRIPTION: The Exp15 `4.4` feasibility pre-check exists, but its warning path is effectively dead. [_allocation_warnings](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L803) is appended to in [_solve_greedy](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L932), but nothing returns it, emits it, or exposes it later. So degraded redundancy is detected but not actually surfaced.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Return warnings from `solve()`, add them to `Allocation` or `RoundResult`, or emit a manager event when a task’s redundancy target is infeasible.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.96  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.91  
DESCRIPTION: [_compute_equivalence_classes](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1591) reclusters the full historical union each round using single-linkage. That lets a later “bridge” finding merge two older classes retroactively, so cumulative class count can go down over time. I reproduced `cum0=2`, then after adding one bridge finding `cum1=1`, `novel1=0`, `kappa_set1=1.0`. That breaks the monotone cumulative-count assumption behind [Y(t)](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L461), [ascending abstraction](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md#L465), and Duane-style diagnostics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Stop reclustering the entire history. Freeze prior equivalence classes, then only match new findings to existing classes or create new ones. A later finding must not be allowed to merge two historical classes.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86  
DESCRIPTION: [_novel_classes](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1665) marks a whole current-round class as non-novel if any member matches prior history. With single-linkage, that can hide genuinely new findings that were grouped with one duplicate. I reproduced a case where round 1 formed one 2-member class, one member matched history, the other did not, and the result was `novel1=0`. Because [process_round](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5089) feeds `_novel_classes()` into diminishing returns and [add_model_round](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L5126), Exp15 `4.6` is not safely closed.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Do novelty at member level against frozen prior classes, or split mixed classes into matched and unmatched portions before computing novelty and yield.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: The no-findings edge case is internally inconsistent. [validate_no_findings](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1844) says empty cumulative findings should not count as converged unless “null expected,” but [converged](/Users/georgejackson/Developer_Projects/Constraint_Engineering/bench/dynamic_management.py#L1772) will return `True` after the minimum rounds because `kappa_set`, `kappa_rate`, and `kappa_adopt` all become `1.0`. I verified `converged(2) == True` for three empty rounds. That makes parser silence or zero-yield rounds look identical to true exhaustion.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an explicit guard in `converged()` such as `observed_signal > 0` or a separate `null_expected` flag, and only allow empty-round convergence when delivery/parsing health is already known to be good.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
